Subject: Marketplace procurement & commercial path

Hi Priya — great speaking with you earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment heading into procurement: 

- Ask: confirm LumenAI procurement preference (PO via invoice vs card), SSO/KMS needs, and whether you intend to purchase via cloud marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure) or direct purchase.
- Marketplace notes: Redwood supports AWS and GCP Marketplace listings today; Azure is on the roadmap (ETA Q3). If marketplace is preferred we can start Marketplace qualification in parallel with security paperwork.
- Commercial path: we commonly see two flows — (1) Pilot on card for quick start (low dollar monthly) then PO+invoice for expansion; or (2) Enterprise contract + PO upfront for Dedicated/Private deployments.

I've attached a short procurement questionnaire to speed review on your side (Procurement_Questionnaire_LumenAI.xlsx). Can you confirm:
1) Preferred procurement method (PO vs card)?
2) Which cloud marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure) you prefer for procurement and billing?
3) Any internal vendor approval hurdles or timelines (e.g., req for W-9, PO terms > net30, review cycles)?

Next steps: if you confirm marketplace interest (AWS or GCP) we’ll loop in our Marketplace onboarding specialist and share the AWS listing checklist and estimated timeline (typically 4–6 weeks once security docs are accepted). If PO is required, we’ll share invoicing steps and sample SOW for signature.

Thanks — I’ll hold off on sending the SOW until we confirm your preferred path.

Best,

Hi Camila — thanks for the recap and the questionnaire. Quick answers from my side and procurement loop: 

1) Procurement preference: for pilots we prefer to use card (to move fast). For anything that will be an ongoing subscription or higher spend we’ll request a PO and invoice. Our procurement team typically requires PO for commitments > $25k/year.
2) Marketplace: we would prefer AWS Marketplace if possible (we also use GCP but AWS is the primary procurement channel for platform/vendor purchases today).
3) Vendor hurdles: procurement will need a W-9, standard enterprise T&Cs review (we usually redline within 7–10 business days), and SOC 2 Type II report for security evaluation. Timing: procurement says they can start review this week if we send the vendor packet and the questionnaire.

CC’d procurement—Sasha will be the point of contact for vendor onboarding. Sasha, can you confirm required documents and whether we can accept an invoice/PO flow for initial pilots below the $25k threshold?

Thanks,
Priya
Product Lead, Integrations | LumenAI

- Pilot vs Enterprise billing: for Hosted API (our cloud offering) we can accept card for pilots and will set up invoicing/PO for enterprise customers after credit checks and an initial contract. For Dedicated/Private deployments we typically require a PO + signed SOW.

- Docs: attaching the AWS Marketplace onboarding checklist and a draft SOW for your procurement team to review (SOW_Redwood-LumenAI_v1.docx). I’ve also included the procurement questionnaire you completed.

- Security: we can share our SOC 2 Type II report and other security artifacts once the procurement email confirms the appropriate distribution list — Sasha, please let me know the secure email/portal you prefer.

3) Redwood to prepare Marketplace listing draft and coordinate pricing model for AWS (expect preliminary listing terms in ~2 weeks).
